assessments.reasoning: The exact §14.3.1.2 LexicalBinding : BindingIdentifier algorithm resolves the binding and performs InitializeReferencedBinding(lhs, undefined). The operation delegates to the environment record’s InitializeBinding. The binding transitions to initialized with the language value undefined at evaluation. Declarative Environment Record initialization marks it initialized, while a separate operation raises ReferenceError for a read while uninitialized. The normative algorithm provides the result independently of the explanatory note. The ordinary let identifier lacks an initializer and its LexicalBinding is actually evaluated. A bare ordinary const is excluded by the early error. Loop ForDeclaration binding uses nextValue in the loop algorithm. The pre-evaluation read can raise ReferenceError. The initializer-free ordinary production initializes to undefined; a loop declaration initializes through nextValue and another grammar route. The copyright corrigendum changes no applicable semantics.

challenge.method: Trace pre-evaluation access, explicit initialization, and the initializer-free identifier in a lexical for-of binding. Check both normal declaration evaluation and the environment record operations, then examine the edition corrigendum.
challenge.results: The pre-evaluation read can raise ReferenceError. The initializer-free ordinary production initializes to undefined; a loop declaration initializes through nextValue and another grammar route. The copyright corrigendum changes no applicable semantics.

limitations: Initialization at evaluation does not imply access before evaluation or describe loop binding initialization.
No conclusion about access before evaluation, explicit initializer evaluation, destructuring, or iteration-time initialization.
This is a specification obligation. It does not independently attest to browser or other implementation conformance.
